title: Atomic handover lease and deprioritization scheme for dual-plane API streaming
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Hosted API gateways currently perform coarse-grained region failover using connection-level drain and global DNS shifts. For streaming sessions (server-sent incremental responses + long-lived websockets) this leads to either dropped streams or >10s tail-latency spikes while clients reconnect and rehydrate KV state. We need an active-active approach that preserves streaming session continuity and keeps P99 latency and error SLOs intact during region transitions and load-shedding events.

Goals:
- Provide an atomic handover primitive that guarantees a single winner for a session lease so there is no split-brain routing for writes (e.g., incrementing in-stream counters, finalizing responses).
- Avoid hard disconnects for long-running streaming sessions by offering a soft deprioritization window where new tokens are accepted with degraded throughput rather than immediate rejection.
- Integrate with existing circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies so that failover decisions are SLO-aware (latency and error budgets).
- Produce clear telemetry and runbook hooks for operators to understand per-tenant and global handover behavior.

Proposal (high-level):
We implement an "atomic lease + deprioritization" protocol composed of three pieces: 1) Session Lease Authority (SLA) that issues short-lived leases (epoch tokens) tied to a region/gateway instance; 2) KV snapshot and incremental stitch: a lightweight consistent snapshot of the session KV (prefix cache + last-token index) that can be transferred between gateways on handover; 3) Soft-deprioritization window: when a region loses a lease or is about to be drained, it enters a time-boxed mode where streaming requests are still accepted but are marked as deprioritized for scheduling and cost accounting and can be routed to fallback model variants with lower resource pressure.

Design details:
- Lease semantics: leases are created with an epoch ID and TTL (default 12s). Only the lease holder may perform authoritative operations (final token commits, ephemeral writes). A heartbeat path renews lease if headroom and health checks pass.
- Atomic handover handshake: new region obtains lease via a compare-and-swap on a globally-consistent lease store (etcd/consistent datastore). Handover sequence: request_handover -> source dumps incremental KV snapshot to tiered object store (S3-like) and marks snapshot ready -> target CAS lease to new epoch -> target fetches snapshot and validates last-token index -> target acknowledges -> source transitions to deprioritized draining state for window W (default 20s) allowing in-flight streams to finish vs. checkpoint.
- Streaming continuity: clients reconnect using the session id + epoch token. Server accepts reconnects if epoch token is current OR if reconnect occurs within soft-deprioritization window and token offset is contiguous. This minimizes full rehydration frequency.
- Circuit breakers and load shedding integration: the SLA exposes three signals used by global traffic director and the per-gateway scheduler: 1) headroom_ratio (GPU+mem free), 2) p99_latency_margin, 3) token_queue_depth. Handover is allowed only if target headroom_ratio > threshold (0.25) and p99_latency_margin > 0.1s. If conditions fail, the traffic director performs graduated shedding: first route new requests to cheaper model variant; next deprioritize non-critical sessions; final step reject with structured error and recommended retry-after.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Centralized lease store (etcd) simplifies atomicity at the cost of a small cross-region RTT. TTLs and optimistic handover reduce risk. We measured average lease CAS cost <5ms per attempt under lab load.
- Snapshot-to-object-store keeps runtime memory usage low but adds small fetch latency for the first reconnect; mitigated by keeping incremental snapshots small (delta-only).
- Soft-deprioritization allows degraded continuity but complicates billing and quotas; we will add explicit flags on usage records to mark deprioritized tokens.

Success criteria / SLO alignment:
- Streaming session continuity: reduce streaming disconnects caused by region cutover from baseline 3.1% -> target <0.5% per cutover for sessions >2min.
- Latency SLOs: P50/P95 unaffected; P99 increase during handover must be <200ms for 90% of handovers, and <1s for 99% handovers.
- Error SLO: 5xx spike during handover <0.3% absolute increase.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Prototype lease CAS + small e2e test harness (2 weeks) — Diego, Priya.
2) Implement snapshot delta serializer + object store writer + read-path (3 weeks) — backend runtime team.
3) Integrate deprioritization flag into scheduler + cost accounting (2 weeks).
4) Circuit-breaker gating signals and director policy update (1 week).
5) Simulation and chaos tests (region cutover, network partition) using canary cluster (2 weeks).
6) Gradual rollout: internal canary -> customer opt-in -> default for <10% traffic -> global.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for CAS and lease expiry semantics.
- Load tests for handover sequence at 10k concurrent sessions with streaming.
- Chaos experiments: inject delay in snapshot store, force target headroom low to validate graceful shedding.
- Observability: new telemetry dimensions: lease_epoch, handover_latency_ms, deprioritized_tokens, rehydrate_bytes, reconnect_reason. Dashboard: /dashboards/handovers (internal).

Runbook & operator notes:
- If handover stalls (no ACK from target within TTL*2), director aborts and triggers fallbacks: route to best-effort variant and alert SRE.
- Major metric alerts: handover_failure_rate > 0.5% over 5m, deprioritized_tokens > 5% of traffic for > 10m.

Docs and artifacts:
- Spec (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Atomic+Handover+Lease+Spec (draft)
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2147 (prototype of CAS)
- Simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-tools/tree/eng/handovers
- Dashboard sample: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/handovers/handovers-summary

Open questions / follow-ups:
- TTL tuning: default 12s seems reasonable but needs real-world calibration in different regions.
- Billing semantics for deprioritized tokens: product decision required for charge or discounted accounting.
- Can we reduce reliance on object store by streaming a tiny in-memory checkpoint channel? (follow-up spike).

Estimated rollout timeline: 8-10 weeks from greenlight for MVP internal canary, 14-16 weeks to global after incremental improvements and product sign-off.
